You are ML Intern, an ML engineering assistant with 18 tools for training, fine-tuning, data processing, inference, and evaluation on the Hugging Face (HF) ecosystem. Your goal is to complete what the user requested with zero errors. You are fully autonomous — research, validate, implement, and deliver results without asking for unnecessary confirmation. # Your knowledge of HF libraries is outdated You do not know current APIs for TRL, Transformers, PEFT, Trackio, or other HF libraries. Your internal knowledge WILL produce wrong imports, wrong argument names, and wrong trainer configurations. Before writing any ML implementation code, start from the literature. The parallel research sub-agents can crawl papers, read their methodology sections, trace citation graphs, and extract the exact datasets and training recipes that produced published results. This is your primary advantage — use it. Your default workflow for any ML task: 1. Find the landmark paper(s) for the task or domain 2. Crawl their citation graphs to find recent downstream work 3. Read methodology sections (not abstracts) of the most promising papers — especially recent ones with strong results, lot of citations, and publications in high-impact conferences 4. Extract the recipe: what dataset, what training method, what hyperparameters produced those results 5. Validate and use those datasets for training ``` research({"task": "Literature crawl for [task]. Start from [paper/topic]. Crawl citation graph for recent downstream papers. Read their methodology sections (3, 4, 5) — extract the exact datasets, training methods, and hyperparameters that produced their best results. Attribute every finding to a specific result (e.g. 'Dataset X + method Y → 85.3% on benchmark Z'). Also find working code examples using current TRL/Transformers APIs.", "context": "User wants to [goal]. We need the best training recipe backed by published results."}) ``` The sub-agent knows how to use github_find_examples, github_read_file, explore_hf_docs, fetch_hf_docs, hf_inspect_dataset, and hf_papers (with citation_graph, read_paper, snippet_search, find_datasets). Be specific in your task description — name anchor papers or arxiv IDs when you have them. You can also call research tools directly (explore_hf_docs, github_read_file, etc.) for quick lookups. Skip research only for trivial non-code operations. # Mistakes you WILL make without research HALLUCINATED IMPORTS: You will import from modules that were renamed or removed. Example: old TRL trainer class names, deprecated Transformers APIs, wrong trackio config field names. Fix: read a current example script first. WRONG TRAINER ARGUMENTS: You will pass configuration arguments that don't exist in current trainer versions. Fix: fetch the actual trainer/config docs via explore_hf_docs + fetch_hf_docs. WRONG DATASET FORMAT: You will assume column names without checking. Training fails with KeyError. Fix: call hf_inspect_dataset or hub_repo_details and verify columns match the training method. DEFAULT TIMEOUT KILLS JOBS: You will leave timeout at the default 30m for training jobs. Training takes hours. The job gets killed and all progress is lost. Fix: set timeout based on model size (minimum 2h for any training). LOST MODELS: You will forget push_to_hub=True and hub_model_id in training config. Job storage is ephemeral — the filesystem is deleted when the job ends. Without push_to_hub, the trained model is permanently lost. BATCH FAILURES: You will submit all ablation/batch jobs at once without testing that one works first. All will fail for the same bug. Fix: submit ONE job first, verify it completes successfully, then submit the rest. SILENT DATASET SUBSTITUTION: When a requested dataset fails to load, you will silently switch to a different one without telling the user. Fix: if the requested dataset isn't available, tell the user and ask what to do. PREFER HUB KERNELS OVER COMPILING ATTENTION: Do NOT pip install 'flash-attn' to enable flash_attention_2 building from source can take many minutes to hours and often fails on the job's CUDA/PyTorch combo. Instead, use the HF `kernels` library (`pip install kernels`, already pulled in by recent TRL) and load a prebuilt attention kernel from the Hub via `attn_implementation`. Examples: `AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(..., attn_implementation="kernels-community/flash-attn2")`, or `kernels-community/vllm-flash-attn3`, or `kernels-community/paged-attention`. With TRL/SFT scripts you can pass `--attn_implementation kernels-community/flash-attn2` on the CLI. Search additional kernels at https://huggingface.co/models?other=kernel. Only `pip install` extra packages (and document why) when no Hub kernel covers the need. SCOPE-CHANGING FIXES: Avoid at all costs! When you hit an error (especially OOM), you will try "creative" workarounds that change what the user asked for and/or change the training task itself — switching full SFT to LoRA on OOM, reducing max_length (silently truncates training data and changes what the model learns), disabling monitoring instead of fixing it. Do not do this. Fix errors with the minimal change that preserves the user's original request and are grounded in research and examples. If the original approach genuinely cannot work, explain why and ask the user for input before changing methods, sequence length, training approach or any other part of the task. # When writing ML code Required sequence before any training/fine-tuning/inference script: 1. Use `research` tool to find working examples, read docs, and get current API patterns 2. Validate dataset: hf_inspect_dataset or hub_repo_details to confirm column names and format 3. Validate model: hub_repo_details to confirm model exists, correct architecture/size/tokenizer Training logging: always set disable_tqdm=True, logging_strategy="steps", and logging_first_step=True in your TrainingArguments/SFTConfig so loss values are printed as plain text lines you can grep, not hidden inside tqdm progress bars. Dataset format requirements by training method: SFT: "messages", "text", or "prompt"/"completion" DPO: "prompt", "chosen", "rejected" GRPO: "prompt" # Trackio Trackio is natively integrated with Transformers Trainer and all TRL trainers — the built-in TrackioCallback handles init/log/finish. In TrainingArguments/SFTConfig/DPOConfig/GRPOConfig set: report_to="trackio" run_name="" # e.g. "sft_qwen3-4b_lr2e-5_bs128" project="" # keeps related runs grouped so you can compare them trackio_space_id="/ml-intern-<8-char-id>" # creates a public dashboard Space `project` and `trackio_space_id` can also be set via TRACKIO_PROJECT / TRACKIO_SPACE_ID env vars. Alerts are how iterations decide what to change. Use trackio.alert(title, text, level) at every decision point in training. Levels: ERROR — stop and change approach (divergence, NaN, OOM) WARN — tweak hyperparameters (overfitting, early stopping, KL spike, reward collapse, slow convergence) INFO — milestones (training complete, target reached, checkpoint saved) Always include numeric values and an actionable suggestion in `text`, e.g. "loss=12.4 at step 200 — lr likely too high, try ×0.1". A future call must be able to parse it and act on it. To add alerts under Trainer/SFTTrainer/GRPOTrainer, pass a custom TrainerCallback via `callbacks=[...]` that calls trackio.alert() inside `on_log` (training metrics like loss, reward, kl) and `on_evaluate` (eval metrics — only available here, not in `on_log`). Keep each `if` simple: one metric, one threshold. Conditions stay easy to adjust between runs. Read alerts back between runs instead of parsing thousands of metric values. CLI — always use --json: trackio get alerts --project

--run --json trackio get alerts --project

--since --json # incremental polling trackio get run --project

--run --json trackio get metric --project

--run --metric --json trackio list runs --project

--json Python: api = trackio.Api(); api.alerts(

, run=, since=); api.runs(

) (each run has .name, .config, .alerts()). Drive the next config from prior alerts: diverged → lr × 0.1 overfitting → weight_decay × 10 or reduce capacity early stopping → lr × 0.5 or adjust schedule high accuracy → refine around current config Read prior config via api.runs(...).config and only mutate keys the alerts justify changing. # Data audit Before working with any dataset, audit it first. Do not assume you know what the data looks like — inspect it. Use hf_inspect_dataset to check: schema/columns, number of rows per split, value distributions for key columns, sample rows. Surface anything notable: class imbalance, missing values, unexpected formats, outliers, duplicate rows, etc. Looking at data is the best way to boost performance of any ML model plus it reduces the likelihood of failed jobs later. # When submitting a training job Before calling hf_jobs, output a pre-flight check: - Reference implementation: [which example you based this on] - Dataset format verified: [columns confirmed via hf_inspect_dataset/hub_repo_details] - push_to_hub=True and hub_model_id set - timeout: [value] (based on: [model size] on [hardware]) - Trackio monitoring included and deploying metrics to a public Space If you cannot fill in all items, stop and complete the missing steps first. For batch/ablation jobs: submit ONE job first. Check logs to confirm it starts training successfully. Only then submit the remaining jobs. Never submit all at once. Hardware sizing: 1-3B params: a10g-largex2 7-13B params: a100-large 30B+ params: l40sx4 or a100x4 70B+ params: a100x8 Note: a10g-small and a10g-large have the SAME 24GB GPU memory. The difference is CPU/RAM only. # Sandbox-first development A private cpu-basic sandbox is already available for normal code execution in each session. For non-trivial scripts, develop and test there before launching via hf_jobs: write script → pip install → test with small run using bash/read/write/edit → fix errors → launch via hf_jobs at scale Do NOT call sandbox_create before normal CPU work. Call sandbox_create only when you need GPU hardware or another non-default sandbox tier. Use GPU sandbox (t4-small minimum) when testing code that uses CUDA, bf16, or model loading. CPU sandboxes cannot test GPU code paths. # When a task has 3+ steps Use plan_tool to track progress. One task in_progress at a time. Mark completed immediately after finishing. Update frequently to show the user what you're doing. # Error recovery When something fails: - Diagnose the actual error. Read the full error message and logs. - Do not retry the exact same thing. Identify what needs to change. - If an API/import error: check documentation for the correct API. - If an OOM error: (1) reduce per_device_train_batch_size and increase gradient_accumulation_steps proportionally to keep effective batch size identical, (2) enable gradient_checkpointing=True, (3) upgrade to larger GPU (a10gx4→a100→a100x4→a100x8). Do NOT switch training methods (e.g. SFT→LoRA) or reduce max_length — those change what the user gets. If OOM happens in sandbox, create a new sandbox with larger GPU hardware. - Never change the user's requested approach (training method, dataset, model, sequence length) without explicit approval. - If a tool call fails repeatedly for the same reason: stop and try a different approach. - Never silently substitute resources (datasets, models) — tell the user if something isn't available. # Task completion Before ending your turn, verify: - Did you actually DO what the user asked, not just explain what you would do? - If something failed: did you diagnose and fix it, or at minimum explain what went wrong and ask for user input? - For training jobs: did you include a working Trackio dashboard URL? Do not stop after describing what you plan to do. Continue calling tools until the task is verifiably done. Do not mark plan tasks as completed if they failed or are only partially done. # Autonomous / headless mode When running autonomously (no human in the loop), you MUST follow these rules: NEVER respond with only text. Every response MUST include at least one tool call. If you have nothing to do, check the plan, verify outputs or plan ahead. A text-only response ends the agent loop permanently — there is no human to re-prompt you. NEVER STOP WORKING. Do NOT decide you are "done" while time remains. The human is not watching — they expect you to use the ENTIRE time budget productively. Do NOT ask "should I continue?" or "is this a good stopping point?" — there is nobody to answer. You run until the timer expires or you are manually killed. Your workflow is a loop, not a checklist. Once you have a working result, KEEP ITERATING: LOOP UNTIL TIME RUNS OUT: 1. Research the approach (read docs, find examples, check current APIs) 2. Implement the solution (write code, set up training) 3. Train and evaluate 4. Save the model to the required output location / push it to Hugging Face Hub 5. Improve: tune hyperparameters, try different data, adjust the training recipe, try a different approach entirely 6. Go to step 1 HYPERPARAMETER TUNING: Do not tune hyperparameters by hand one-at-a-time. Write a script that launches a sweep over a grid of values (learning rate, epochs, batch size, etc.) and evaluates each run automatically. One well-designed sweep script beats ten manual experiments. If you run out of ideas: go back to the literature. Crawl citation graphs deeper — find papers you haven't read yet, read their methodology sections, extract new datasets or training tricks. Look for papers that cite your current approach and improved on it. Try combining recipes from different papers. Re-read the task prompt for angles you missed. Re-read the training logs for clues. There is always a paper you haven't read yet, and it probably has a better dataset. Check the remaining time periodically with the timer command specified in the task prompt. Budget your time: reserve at least 10 minutes at the end for final evaluation and model saving. The task is NOT done until: - The required output exists (e.g. final model, metrics reached, dataset updated etc) - You have evaluated the model and confirmed it works # Communication - Be concise and direct. No filler, no restating what the user said. - One-word answers when appropriate for simple questions. - Always include direct Hub URLs when referencing models, datasets, Spaces, or jobs. - For errors: state what went wrong, why, and what you're doing to fix it. - Do not over-explain or present elaborate option menus for simple tasks. When the user's intent is clear, act on it. Present options only when there's genuine ambiguity. - Use the `notify` tool only when the user explicitly asked for out-of-band notifications or when the task clearly requires reporting to a configured messaging destination. Do not use it for routine chat updates. # Tool usage - Execute multiple independent tool calls in parallel when possible. - HF_TOKEN is automatically available in job secrets — no need to include it extra. - For training monitoring: include Trackio in the script and provide the dashboard URL. - For private/gated datasets: HF_TOKEN is needed — it's auto-loaded into job secrets. # CLI / Local mode You are running as a local CLI tool on the user's machine. There is NO sandbox — bash, read, write, and edit operate directly on the local filesystem. Working directory: /root/v2rmp Use absolute paths or paths relative to the working directory. Do NOT use /app/ paths — that is a sandbox convention that does not apply here. The sandbox_create tool is NOT available. Run code directly with bash. 1	//! Route quality predictor.
     2	//!
     3	//! Predicts expected gap to optimal and tour length *before* solving,
     4	//! allowing early stopping or solver spawning decisions.
     5	//!
     6	//! Architecture: 28 → 64 → 32 → 2  (gap %, tour length km)
     7	//!
     8	//! Research basis: RouteFinder encoder + gap prediction (2406.15007)
     9	
    10	use crate::core::ml::features::InstanceFeatures;
    11	use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
    12	
    13	/// Predicted route quality metrics.
    14	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    15	pub struct QualityPrediction {
    16	    /// Predicted gap to optimal tour length (%).
    17	    pub predicted_gap_pct: f64,
    18	    /// Predicted absolute tour length (km).
    19	    pub predicted_tour_length_km: f64,
    20	    /// Confidence score [0,1] (if calibrated).
    21	    pub confidence: f64,
    22	}
    23	
    24	/// Predict quality from instance features.
    25	///
    26	/// Currently returns heuristic estimates.  A learned MLP can be loaded
    27	/// from safetensors in the same pattern as `selector.rs`.
    28	pub fn predict_quality(features: &InstanceFeatures) -> QualityPrediction {
    29	    // Heuristic fallback: more stops + more spread → higher gap.
    30	    let gap = (features.n_stops_norm * 20.0
    31	        + features.density_norm * 10.0
    32	        + features.knn_diameter_norm * 5.0)
    33	        .min(50.0);
    34	
    35	    // Rough tour length lower bound (star tour heuristic)
    36	    let tour_est = features.dist_mean_norm * 100.0 * features.n_stops_norm * 500.0;
    37	
    38	    QualityPrediction {
    39	        predicted_gap_pct: gap,
    40	        predicted_tour_length_km: tour_est,
    41	        confidence: 0.5,
    42	    }
    43	}

1	# v2rmp ML/AI Integration Architecture
     2	
     3	## Executive Summary
     4	
     5	This document describes the heavy ML/AI integration into v2rmp (rmpca), a Rust CLI/TUI/GUI tool for route optimization. The integration upgrades the existing rule-based ML modules to learned models, adds graph embeddings, route quality prediction, NLP query parsing, and AutoML hyperparameter tuning — all backed by published research.
     6	
     7	## Current State (Audit)
     8	
     9	### Existing ML/AI Touchpoints
    10	
    11	| Module | File | Current Capabilities | Gap |
    12	|--------|------|---------------------|-----|
    13	| `ml` | `src/core/ml.rs` | Rule-based solver selection (`predict_solver`), route quality scoring (`score_route`), 12-dim feature vectors (`route_feature_vector`) | No learned model — purely heuristic scoring. No training pipeline. |
    14	| `embed` | `src/core/embed.rs` | BERT text embeddings via Candle (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5) | Only batch text embed. No semantic search index, no fine-tuning. |
    15	| MCP Server | `src/bin/rmpca-mcp-server.rs` | 15+ tools incl. `predict_solver`, `score_route`, `route_embedding` | `predict_solver` returns heuristic scores, not learned predictions. |
    16	| VRP Solvers | `src/core/vrp/solvers/*.rs` | 5 classical heuristics (Clarke-Wright, Sweep, 2-Opt, Or-Opt, Default) | No neural solver, no learned local search guidance. |
    17	| Elevation | `src/core/elevation/` | DEM GeoTIFF queries, fuel estimation | No ML-based terrain-aware weighting. |
    18	
    19	### Architecture Gaps
    20	
    21	1. **No learned solver selector** — `predict_solver` uses hand-tuned weights (density > 5.0 → +0.15, etc.). No data-driven training.
    22	2. **No instance-aware AutoML** — solver hyperparameters are hard-coded. No per-instance tuning.
    23	3. **No graph embeddings for road networks** — road segments are treated as raw edges. No learned representations.
    24	4. **No route quality prediction** — quality is only scored *after* solving. No early-stopping or solver-spawning guidance.
    25	5. **No NLP query parser** — the `agent` command takes JSON only. No natural-language routing requests.
    26	6. **No learned local search guidance** — 2-Opt/Or-Opt use random/exhaustive moves. No neural move selector.
    27	
    28	---
    29	
    30	## Proposed Architecture
    31	
    32	### Module Map
    33	
    34	```
    35	src/core/
    36	├── ml/                          # NEW: ML module directory
    37	│   ├── mod.rs                   # Re-exports, shared types
    38	│   ├── selector.rs              # Neural/ensemble solver selector
    39	│   ├── features.rs              # Instance feature extraction (research-backed)
    40	│   ├── quality_predictor.rs     # Route quality prediction before solve
    41	│   ├── automl.rs                # Instance-aware hyperparameter regression
    42	│   └── graph_embed.rs           # Road network graph embeddings
    43	├── embed.rs                     # EXISTING: text embeddings (BERT)
    44	├── nlp.rs                       # NEW: NL query → VRP config parser
    45	├── vrp/                         # EXISTING
    46	│   ├── solvers/
    47	│   │   ├── neural_guided.rs     # NEW: neural-guided local search wrapper
    48	│   │   └── ...
    49	│   └── ...
    50	└── ...
    51	```
    52	
    53	### 1. Neural Solver Selector (`ml::selector`)
    54	
    55	**Replaces**: `src/core/ml.rs::predict_solver()`  
    56	**Research basis**: Instance-Aware Parameter Configuration (2605.00572, 2026) + RouteFinder (2406.15007, 2024)
    57	
    58	**Design**:
    59	- **Feature extraction**: 28-dim instance feature vector (see `ml::features`).
    60	- **Model**: Small MLP (2 hidden layers, 128→64→5) implemented in Candle.
    61	- **Output**: Softmax over 5 solver IDs + confidence.
    62	- **Training**: Offline on CVRPLIB + synthetic instances. Labels = best solver in fixed time budget.
    63	- **Inference**: ~0.1ms per instance (pure Rust/Candle).
    64	
    65	**Feature vector (28-dim)**:
    66	```
    67	# Geometric (8)
    68	n_stops_norm, n_vehicles_norm, avg_pairwise_km_norm, lat_spread_norm,
    69	lon_spread_norm, density_norm, area_km2_norm, depot_centroid_dist_norm
    70	
    71	# Graph (8) — from kNN(k=10) graph of stops
    72	knn_avg_degree, knn_max_degree, knn_clustering, knn_diameter_norm,
    73	knn_mst_weight_norm, knn_avg_shortest_path, knn_spectral_gap, knn_assortativity
    74	
    75	# Demand (4)
    76	total_demand_norm, demand_std_norm, tight_capacity_flag, capacity_ratio
    77	
    78	# Distance matrix stats (4)
    79	dist_mean_norm, dist_std_norm, dist_skewness, depot_dist_mean_norm
    80	
    81	# Objective & interaction (4)
    82	objective_onehot[4], stops_per_vehicle_norm, spread_x_demand_interaction
    83	```
    84	
    85	### 2. Instance-Aware AutoML (`ml::automl`)
    86	
    87	**Replaces**: hard-coded solver hyperparameters  
    88	**Research basis**: Instance-Aware Parameter Configuration (2605.00572)
    89	
    90	**Design**:
    91	- **Problem**: Predict best hyperparameters (e.g., `max_iterations`, `temperature` for SA, `tabu_tenure`) given instance features.
    92	- **Model**: Separate Ridge regression per hyperparameter, or a single multi-output MLP.
    93	- **Training**: Run `irace`-style offline tuning on a diverse instance set, record best configs, train regressor.
    94	- **Usage**: Before solving, extract features → predict hyperparameters → inject into solver.
    95	
    96	### 3. Route Quality Predictor (`ml::quality_predictor`)
    97	
    98	**New capability**  
    99	**Research basis**: RouteFinder encoder + gap prediction
   100	
   101	**Design**:
   102	- **Input**: Instance features (same 28-dim vector).
   103	- **Output**: Predicted gap to optimal (%) and expected tour length (km).
   104	- **Model**: Small MLP (28→64→32→2) in Candle.
   105	- **Usage**:
   106	  - Early stopping: if predicted gap < threshold, skip expensive local search.
   107	  - Solver spawning: if predicted quality of default solver is poor, automatically spawn Or-Opt.
   108	
   109	### 4. Graph Embeddings for Road Networks (`ml::graph_embed`)
   110	
   111	**New capability**  
   112	**Research basis**: GAIN (2107.07791) + RRNCO (2503.16159)
   113	
   114	**Design**:
   115	- **Representation**: Line-graph of OSM road network (roads → nodes, junctions → edges).
   116	- **Features per road segment**: length, speed limit, road class one-hot, geometry sinuosity, elevation variance.
   117	- **Model**: 2-layer GraphSAGE-MEAN (Candle) or pre-trained PyTorch → ONNX → Candle.
   118	- **Usage**: Fused into distance/duration matrix for VRP. Edge weights become `haversine * (1 + learned_factor)`.
   119	
   120	### 5. NLP Query Parser (`nlp`)
   121	
   122	**New capability**  
   123	**Research basis**: From Words to Routes (2403.10795)
   124	
   125	**Design**:
   126	- **Approach**: Small fine-tuned LLM (Qwen2.5-1.5B or similar) served via Candle, or rule-based NLU + entity extraction.
   127	- **Input**: "Route 50 packages with 5 vans starting at 45.5,-73.6 by 5pm"
   128	- **Output**: JSON VRP config (`{"num_stops":50,"num_vehicles":5,"depot":[45.5,-73.6],"deadline":"17:00"}`).
   129	- **Training**: Synthetic SFT dataset (template utterances → JSON).
   130	- **Integration**: New `agent` task type `NlpParse`, new MCP tool `parse_routing_query`.
   131	
   132	### 6. Neural-Guided Local Search (`vrp::solvers::neural_guided`)
   133	
   134	**New capability**  
   135	**Research basis**: RLOR (2303.13117) + Analytics & ML in VRP survey (2102.10012)
   136	
   137	**Design**:
   138	- **Wrapper**: Wraps existing 2-Opt / Or-Opt solvers with a neural move selector.
   139	- **Move representation**: For each candidate edge swap, encode the local subgraph (4 nodes + edges) as a feature vector.
   140	- **Model**: Tiny MLP that scores each candidate move. Pick top-k instead of exhaustive/random.
   141	- **Training**: REINFORCE / PPO on synthetic instances where reward = improvement in tour length.
   142	
   143	---
   144	
   145	## Data Flow
   146	
   147	```
   148	User Input
   149	    ├── NLP Query ──→ nlp::parse() ──→ VRP Config JSON
   150	    │
   151	    └── JSON Task ──→ agent::run()
   152	                        │
   153	                        ▼
   154	            Extract ──→ Clean ──→ Compile ──→ Optimize
   155	                │                           │
   156	                ▼                           ▼
   157	        ml::graph_embed()           ml::features::extract()
   158	                │                           │
   159	                ▼                           ▼
   160	        Edge embeddings           selector::predict()
   161	                                        │
   162	                                        ▼
   163	                              quality_predictor::predict()
   164	                                        │
   165	                                        ▼
   166	                              automl::tune_hyperparams()
   167	                                        │
   168	                                        ▼
   169	                              Spawn best solver + best params
   170	                                        │
   171	                                        ▼
   172	                              score_route() → feedback loop
   173	```
   174	
   175	---
   176	
   177	## MCP Server Integration
   178	
   179	### New MCP Tools
   180	
   181	| Tool | Description | Model |
   182	|------|-------------|-------|
   183	| `predict_solver` | **Upgraded** — learned ensemble selector | MLP (Candle) |
   184	| `predict_quality` | Predict expected gap / tour length before solving | MLP (Candle) |
   185	| `tune_hyperparams` | Predict best hyperparameters for this instance | Ridge/MLP |
   186	| `graph_embed_network` | Embed a road network (.rmp or GeoJSON) | GraphSAGE |
   187	| `parse_routing_query` | NL → structured VRP config | Small LLM / NLU |
   188	| `neural_vrp_solve` | Solve VRP with neural constructive heuristic | RouteFinder-style |
   189	
   190	### Existing Tool Upgrades
   191	
   192	| Tool | Change |
   193	|------|--------|
   194	| `predict_solver` | Replace rule-based with learned model; add `use_model` flag |
   195	| `score_route` | Add predicted-vs-actual gap for feedback logging |
   196	| `route_embedding` | Expand from 12-dim to 28-dim research-backed features |
   197	
   198	---
   199	
   200	## Training & Model Lifecycle
   201	
   202	### Offline Training (Python → Rust)
   203	
   204	```
   205	1. Generate / download training data
   206	   - CVRPLIB instances (http://vrp.atd-lab.inf.puc-rio.br/)
   207	   - Synthetic instances (Kool et al. 2019 generator)
   208	   - OSM road networks (osmnx)
   209	
   210	2. Label instances
   211	   - Run all 5 solvers × 20 hyperparam configs per instance
   212	   - Record best solver, best params, achieved gap
   213	
   214	3. Train models (PyTorch / XGBoost)
   215	   - Solver selector: LightGBM or small MLP
   216	   - Quality predictor: Ridge / MLP

Here is a comprehensive summary of the ML/AI functions in the v2rmp codebase, based on my reading of the source files:

## ML/AI Functions Overview

The project has a two-tier ML system:

1. **Legacy rule-based** (`src/core/ml_legacy.rs`) — deterministic heuristics, always works
2. **New learned modules** (`src/core/ml/`) — Candle-based neural models that load from safetensors; gracefully fall back to legacy if model files are missing

---

### 1. Neural Solver Selector (`ml::selector`)

**Purpose:** Given a VRP instance (stops, vehicles, demands), pick the best solver algorithm from 5 candidates.

**Architecture:** MLP `28 → 128 → 64 → 5` (ReLU hidden, softmax output) implemented in [Candle](https://github.com/huggingface/candle) (Hugging Face's Rust ML framework).

**Input:** `InstanceFeatures` — a 28-dimensional normalized vector extracted from the VRP instance (see `ml::features` below).

**Output:** `NeuralPrediction` — recommended solver ID + confidence score + runner-up + score distribution across all 5 solvers.

**How it works:**
1. Extract 28 features from the VRP instance
2. Load weights from `models/solver_selector.safetensors` into a `NeuralSelector` struct (3 `Linear` layers)
3. Forward pass: `input → lin1 → ReLU → lin2 → ReLU → lin3 → softmax`
4. Sort probabilities, return top solver
5. **Fallback:** If the safetensors file doesn't exist or inference fails, falls back to `ml_legacy::predict_solver` (rule-based)

---

### 2. Instance Feature Extraction (`ml::features`)

**Purpose:** Convert a raw VRP instance into a fixed 28-dim feature vector suitable for neural network input.

**28 features** (all normalized to ~[0,1]):

| Group | Features | How computed |
|-------|----------|--------------|
| **Geometric (8)** | stops, vehicles, avg pairwise dist, lat/lon spread, density, area, depot-centroid dist | Haversine distances, std dev of coords |
| **Graph (8)** | avg/max degree, clustering, diameter, MST weight, avg shortest path, spectral gap, assortativity | kNN graph (k=10) of stops; Floyd-Warshall for small n, sampling for large n |
| **Demand (4)** | total demand, demand std, tight capacity flag, capacity ratio | Sum/std of stop demands vs vehicle capacity |
| **Distance matrix (4)** | mean, std, skewness, depot mean | Stats on all pairwise haversine distances |
| **Objective (4)** | one-hot for min_distance, min_time, balance_load, min_vehicles | Binary flags from `VrpObjective` enum |

**Key algorithms inside:**
- `knn_graph_features()` — builds k=10 nearest-neighbor graph, computes clustering coefficient, Prim's MST, all-pairs shortest paths (Floyd-Warshall), spectral gap, degree assortativity
- `prim_mst()` — classic Prim's algorithm on distance matrix
- `all_pairs_shortest_paths()` — Floyd-Warshall with diameter + average extraction

---

### 3. Route Quality Predictor (`ml::quality_predictor`)

**Purpose:** Before solving, predict how good the solution will be — useful for early stopping or deciding whether to spawn an expensive metaheuristic.

**Architecture:** Planned: MLP `28 → 64 → 32 → 2`. **Current:** Heuristic fallback (not yet trained).

**Output:** `QualityPrediction`
- `predicted_gap_pct` — estimated gap to optimal tour length (%)
- `predicted_tour_length_km` — rough tour length estimate
- `confidence` — 0.5 (placeholder)

**How it works (current heuristic):**
```rust
gap = (n_stops_norm * 20 + density_norm * 10 + diameter_norm * 5).min(50)
tour_est = dist_mean_norm * 100 * n_stops_norm * 500
```

**Future:** Will load a safetensors model same pattern as `selector.rs`.

---

### 4. AutoML Hyperparameter Tuner (`ml::automl`)

**Purpose:** Predict solver hyperparameters (max iterations, temperature, tabu tenure, cooling rate, neighbourhood radius) tailored to the specific instance.

**Architecture:** Planned: Ridge regression or multi-output MLP per hyperparameter. **Current:** Returns fixed defaults.

**Output:** `SolverHyperparams`
- `max_iterations: 1000`
- `temperature: 100.0`
- `tabu_tenure: 7`
- `cooling_rate: 0.995`
- `neighbourhood_radius: 3`

**How it works (future):**
1. Extract instance features
2. Load Ridge/MLP weights from safetensors
3. Predict per-hyperparameter values
4. Inject into solver before running

---

### 5. Graph Embeddings for Road Networks (`ml::graph_embed`)

**Purpose:** Convert OSM road networks into learned 64-dimensional edge embeddings that can improve VRP distance matrices.

**Architecture:** 2-layer GraphSAGE-MEAN implemented in Candle.
- Input: 10-dim edge features (length, oneway flag + 8 padding)
- Layer 1: `SAGEConv(10 → 64)` 
- Layer 2: `SAGEConv(64 → 64)`

**How GraphSAGE works here:**
1. **Line-graph construction:** Roads become nodes, junctions become edges
2. **Neighbor aggregation:** For each road segment, mean-pool its adjacent road segments' features
3. **SAGEConv forward:** `output = linear_l(self_features) + linear_r(aggregated_neighbors)`
4. Two layers with ReLU between them

**Output:** `Vec<RoadEmbedding>` — one 64-dim vector per road segment.

**Current state:** Falls back to empty embeddings if `models/graph_embed.safetensors` is missing.

---

### 6. NLP Query Parser (`core::nlp`)

**Purpose:** Convert natural language routing requests into structured VRP JSON.

**Two modes:**

**Rule-based** (`parse_query()`) — always available:
- Regex entity extraction: numbers ("50 packages"), coordinates ("45.5,-73.6"), times ("by 5pm"), capacity, speed
- Keyword intent classification: "sweep" → CPP, "time window" → CVRPTW, "package" → CVRP
- Template JSON generation with slot filling

**LLM-based** (`QwenNLParser`, gated behind `feature = "ml"`):
- Loads `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` from Hugging Face Hub via Candle
- System prompt: "Convert routing query to VRP JSON"
- Autoregressive generation with chat template (`<|im_start|>system...user...assistant`)
- 30s timeout, 256 max tokens

---

### 7. Legacy Rule-Based Scoring (`ml_legacy`)

**Purpose:** Deterministic fallback that works without any model files.

**Key functions:**
- `predict_solver()` — Scores 5 solvers with hand-tuned heuristics (density > 5 → default wins, tight capacity → Clarke-Wright, many vehicles → sweep, etc.)
- `score_route()` — Post-solve quality scoring on 4 dimensions:
  - **Distance efficiency** — star-tour lower bound vs actual
  - **Load balance** — max deviation from mean stop count per route
  - **Turn quality** — penalizes U-turns (×2), lefts (×0.3), rights (×0.1)
  - **Coverage** — fraction of stops assigned
  - **Overall** — weighted composite (35/25/20/20)

---

### Data Flow (how they connect)

```
User Input
    │
    ├── NLP Query ──→ nlp::parse_query() ──→ VRP JSON
    │
    └── JSON Task ──→ agent::run()
                        │
                        ▼
            ml::features::InstanceFeatures::from_input(input)
                        │
                        ├──→ ml::selector::predict_solver() ──→ best solver ID
                        │
                        ├──→ ml::quality_predictor::predict_quality() ──→ gap estimate
                        │
                        └──→ ml::automl::predict_hyperparams() ──→ solver params
                                        │
                                        ▼
                              Spawn solver with best config
                                        │
                                        ▼
                              ml_legacy::score_route() ──→ quality feedback
```

### Architecture Philosophy

| Principle | Implementation |
|-----------|----------------|
| **Graceful degradation** | Every learned module falls back to rule-based if model missing |
| **Pure Rust inference** | Candle runs on CPU/CUDA/Metal; no Python runtime needed |
| **Research-backed** | Features drawn from RouteFinder (2024), RRNCO (2025), Instance-Aware Parameter Configuration (2026), GAIN (2021) |
| **Offline training, online inference** | Models trained in Python (PyTorch) → exported to safetensors → loaded by Candle |
| **Deterministic** | No randomness in production inference; fixed seed where needed |

1	# v2rmp ML/AI Integration Architecture
     2	
     3	## Executive Summary
     4	
     5	This document describes the heavy ML/AI integration into v2rmp (rmpca), a Rust CLI/TUI/GUI tool for route optimization. The integration upgrades the existing rule-based ML modules to learned models, adds graph embeddings, route quality prediction, NLP query parsing, and AutoML hyperparameter tuning — all backed by published research.
     6	
     7	## Current State (Audit)
     8	
     9	### Existing ML/AI Touchpoints
    10	
    11	| Module | File | Current Capabilities | Gap |
    12	|--------|------|---------------------|-----|
    13	| `ml` | `src/core/ml.rs` | Rule-based solver selection (`predict_solver`), route quality scoring (`score_route`), 12-dim feature vectors (`route_feature_vector`) | No learned model — purely heuristic scoring. No training pipeline. |
    14	| `embed` | `src/core/embed.rs` | BERT text embeddings via Candle (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5) | Only batch text embed. No semantic search index, no fine-tuning. |
    15	| MCP Server | `src/bin/rmpca-mcp-server.rs` | 15+ tools incl. `predict_solver`, `score_route`, `route_embedding` | `predict_solver` returns heuristic scores, not learned predictions. |
    16	| VRP Solvers | `src/core/vrp/solvers/*.rs` | 5 classical heuristics (Clarke-Wright, Sweep, 2-Opt, Or-Opt, Default) | No neural solver, no learned local search guidance. |
    17	| Elevation | `src/core/elevation/` | DEM GeoTIFF queries, fuel estimation | No ML-based terrain-aware weighting. |
    18	
    19	### Architecture Gaps
    20	
    21	1. **No learned solver selector** — `predict_solver` uses hand-tuned weights (density > 5.0 → +0.15, etc.). No data-driven training.
    22	2. **No instance-aware AutoML** — solver hyperparameters are hard-coded. No per-instance tuning.
    23	3. **No graph embeddings for road networks** — road segments are treated as raw edges. No learned representations.
    24	4. **No route quality prediction** — quality is only scored *after* solving. No early-stopping or solver-spawning guidance.
    25	5. **No NLP query parser** — the `agent` command takes JSON only. No natural-language routing requests.
    26	6. **No learned local search guidance** — 2-Opt/Or-Opt use random/exhaustive moves. No neural move selector.
    27	
    28	---
    29	
    30	## Proposed Architecture
    31	
    32	### Module Map
    33	
    34	```
    35	src/core/
    36	├── ml/                          # NEW: ML module directory
    37	│   ├── mod.rs                   # Re-exports, shared types
    38	│   ├── selector.rs              # Neural/ensemble solver selector
    39	│   ├── features.rs              # Instance feature extraction (research-backed)
    40	│   ├── quality_predictor.rs     # Route quality prediction before solve
    41	│   ├── automl.rs                # Instance-aware hyperparameter regression
    42	│   └── graph_embed.rs           # Road network graph embeddings
    43	├── embed.rs                     # EXISTING: text embeddings (BERT)
    44	├── nlp.rs                       # NEW: NL query → VRP config parser
    45	├── vrp/                         # EXISTING
    46	│   ├── solvers/
    47	│   │   ├── neural_guided.rs     # NEW: neural-guided local search wrapper
    48	│   │   └── ...
    49	│   └── ...
    50	└── ...
    51	```
    52	
    53	### 1. Neural Solver Selector (`ml::selector`)
    54	
    55	**Replaces**: `src/core/ml.rs::predict_solver()`  
    56	**Research basis**: Instance-Aware Parameter Configuration (2605.00572, 2026) + RouteFinder (2406.15007, 2024)
    57	
    58	**Design**:
    59	- **Feature extraction**: 28-dim instance feature vector (see `ml::features`).
    60	- **Model**: Small MLP (2 hidden layers, 128→64→5) implemented in Candle.
    61	- **Output**: Softmax over 5 solver IDs + confidence.
    62	- **Training**: Offline on CVRPLIB + synthetic instances. Labels = best solver in fixed time budget.
    63	- **Inference**: ~0.1ms per instance (pure Rust/Candle).
    64	
    65	**Feature vector (28-dim)**:
    66	```
    67	# Geometric (8)
    68	n_stops_norm, n_vehicles_norm, avg_pairwise_km_norm, lat_spread_norm,
    69	lon_spread_norm, density_norm, area_km2_norm, depot_centroid_dist_norm
    70	
    71	# Graph (8) — from kNN(k=10) graph of stops
    72	knn_avg_degree, knn_max_degree, knn_clustering, knn_diameter_norm,
    73	knn_mst_weight_norm, knn_avg_shortest_path, knn_spectral_gap, knn_assortativity
    74	
    75	# Demand (4)
    76	total_demand_norm, demand_std_norm, tight_capacity_flag, capacity_ratio
    77	
    78	# Distance matrix stats (4)
    79	dist_mean_norm, dist_std_norm, dist_skewness, depot_dist_mean_norm
    80	
    81	# Objective & interaction (4)
    82	objective_onehot[4], stops_per_vehicle_norm, spread_x_demand_interaction
    83	```
    84	
    85	### 2. Instance-Aware AutoML (`ml::automl`)
    86	
    87	**Replaces**: hard-coded solver hyperparameters  
    88	**Research basis**: Instance-Aware Parameter Configuration (2605.00572)
    89	
    90	**Design**:
    91	- **Problem**: Predict best hyperparameters (e.g., `max_iterations`, `temperature` for SA, `tabu_tenure`) given instance features.
    92	- **Model**: Separate Ridge regression per hyperparameter, or a single multi-output MLP.
    93	- **Training**: Run `irace`-style offline tuning on a diverse instance set, record best configs, train regressor.
    94	- **Usage**: Before solving, extract features → predict hyperparameters → inject into solver.
    95	
    96	### 3. Route Quality Predictor (`ml::quality_predictor`)
    97	
    98	**New capability**  
    99	**Research basis**: RouteFinder encoder + gap prediction
   100	
   101	**Design**:
   102	- **Input**: Instance features (same 28-dim vector).
   103	- **Output**: Predicted gap to optimal (%) and expected tour length (km).
   104	- **Model**: Small MLP (28→64→32→2) in Candle.
   105	- **Usage**:
   106	  - Early stopping: if predicted gap < threshold, skip expensive local search.
   107	  - Solver spawning: if predicted quality of default solver is poor, automatically spawn Or-Opt.
   108	
   109	### 4. Graph Embeddings for Road Networks (`ml::graph_embed`)
   110	
   111	**New capability**  
   112	**Research basis**: GAIN (2107.07791) + RRNCO (2503.16159)
   113	
   114	**Design**:
   115	- **Representation**: Line-graph of OSM road network (roads → nodes, junctions → edges).
   116	- **Features per road segment**: length, speed limit, road class one-hot, geometry sinuosity, elevation variance.
   117	- **Model**: 2-layer GraphSAGE-MEAN (Candle) or pre-trained PyTorch → ONNX → Candle.
   118	- **Usage**: Fused into distance/duration matrix for VRP. Edge weights become `haversine * (1 + learned_factor)`.
   119	
   120	### 5. NLP Query Parser (`nlp`)
   121	
   122	**New capability**  
   123	**Research basis**: From Words to Routes (2403.10795)
   124	
   125	**Design**:
   126	- **Approach**: Small fine-tuned LLM (Qwen2.5-1.5B or similar) served via Candle, or rule-based NLU + entity extraction.
   127	- **Input**: "Route 50 packages with 5 vans starting at 45.5,-73.6 by 5pm"
   128	- **Output**: JSON VRP config (`{"num_stops":50,"num_vehicles":5,"depot":[45.5,-73.6],"deadline":"17:00"}`).
   129	- **Training**: Synthetic SFT dataset (template utterances → JSON).
   130	- **Integration**: New `agent` task type `NlpParse`, new MCP tool `parse_routing_query`.
   131	
   132	### 6. Neural-Guided Local Search (`vrp::solvers::neural_guided`)
   133	
   134	**New capability**  
   135	**Research basis**: RLOR (2303.13117) + Analytics & ML in VRP survey (2102.10012)
   136	
   137	**Design**:
   138	- **Wrapper**: Wraps existing 2-Opt / Or-Opt solvers with a neural move selector.
   139	- **Move representation**: For each candidate edge swap, encode the local subgraph (4 nodes + edges) as a feature vector.
   140	- **Model**: Tiny MLP that scores each candidate move. Pick top-k instead of exhaustive/random.
   141	- **Training**: REINFORCE / PPO on synthetic instances where reward = improvement in tour length.

Here is a comprehensive summary of the ML/AI functions in the v2rmp codebase, based on my reading of the source files:

## ML/AI Functions Overview

The project has a two-tier ML system:

1. **Legacy rule-based** (`src/core/ml_legacy.rs`) — deterministic heuristics, always works
2. **New learned modules** (`src/core/ml/`) — Candle-based neural models that load from safetensors; gracefully fall back to legacy if model files are missing

---

### 1. Neural Solver Selector (`ml::selector`)

**Purpose:** Given a VRP instance (stops, vehicles, demands), pick the best solver algorithm from 5 candidates.

**Architecture:** MLP `28 → 128 → 64 → 5` (ReLU hidden, softmax output) implemented in [Candle](https://github.com/huggingface/candle) (Hugging Face's Rust ML framework).

**Input:** `InstanceFeatures` — a 28-dimensional normalized vector extracted from the VRP instance (see `ml::features` below).

**Output:** `NeuralPrediction` — recommended solver ID + confidence score + runner-up + score distribution across all 5 solvers.

**How it works:**
1. Extract 28 features from the VRP instance
2. Load weights from `models/solver_selector.safetensors` into a `NeuralSelector` struct (3 `Linear` layers)
3. Forward pass: `input → lin1 → ReLU → lin2 → ReLU → lin3 → softmax`
4. Sort probabilities, return top solver
5. **Fallback:** If the safetensors file doesn't exist or inference fails, falls back to `ml_legacy::predict_solver` (rule-based)

---

### 2. Instance Feature Extraction (`ml::features`)

**Purpose:** Convert a raw VRP instance into a fixed 28-dim feature vector suitable for neural network input.

**28 features** (all normalized to ~[0,1]):

| Group | Features | How computed |
|-------|----------|--------------|
| **Geometric (8)** | stops, vehicles, avg pairwise dist, lat/lon spread, density, area, depot-centroid dist | Haversine distances, std dev of coords |
| **Graph (8)** | avg/max degree, clustering, diameter, MST weight, avg shortest path, spectral gap, assortativity | kNN graph (k=10) of stops; Floyd-Warshall for small n, sampling for large n |
| **Demand (4)** | total demand, demand std, tight capacity flag, capacity ratio | Sum/std of stop demands vs vehicle capacity |
| **Distance matrix (4)** | mean, std, skewness, depot mean | Stats on all pairwise haversine distances |
| **Objective (4)** | one-hot for min_distance, min_time, balance_load, min_vehicles | Binary flags from `VrpObjective` enum |

**Key algorithms inside:**
- `knn_graph_features()` — builds k=10 nearest-neighbor graph, computes clustering coefficient, Prim's MST, all-pairs shortest paths (Floyd-Warshall), spectral gap, degree assortativity
- `prim_mst()` — classic Prim's algorithm on distance matrix
- `all_pairs_shortest_paths()` — Floyd-Warshall with diameter + average extraction

---

### 3. Route Quality Predictor (`ml::quality_predictor`)

**Purpose:** Before solving, predict how good the solution will be — useful for early stopping or deciding whether to spawn an expensive metaheuristic.

**Architecture:** Planned: MLP `28 → 64 → 32 → 2`. **Current:** Heuristic fallback (not yet trained).

**Output:** `QualityPrediction`
- `predicted_gap_pct` — estimated gap to optimal tour length (%)
- `predicted_tour_length_km` — rough tour length estimate
- `confidence` — 0.5 (placeholder)

**How it works (current heuristic):**
```rust
gap = (n_stops_norm * 20 + density_norm * 10 + diameter_norm * 5).min(50)
tour_est = dist_mean_norm * 100 * n_stops_norm * 500
```

**Future:** Will load a safetensors model same pattern as `selector.rs`.

---

### 4. AutoML Hyperparameter Tuner (`ml::automl`)

**Purpose:** Predict solver hyperparameters (max iterations, temperature, tabu tenure, cooling rate, neighbourhood radius) tailored to the specific instance.

**Architecture:** Planned: Ridge regression or multi-output MLP per hyperparameter. **Current:** Returns fixed defaults.

**Output:** `SolverHyperparams`
- `max_iterations: 1000`
- `temperature: 100.0`
- `tabu_tenure: 7`
- `cooling_rate: 0.995`
- `neighbourhood_radius: 3`

**How it works (future):**
1. Extract instance features
2. Load Ridge/MLP weights from safetensors
3. Predict per-hyperparameter values
4. Inject into solver before running

---

### 5. Graph Embeddings for Road Networks (`ml::graph_embed`)

**Purpose:** Convert OSM road networks into learned 64-dimensional edge embeddings that can improve VRP distance matrices.

**Architecture:** 2-layer GraphSAGE-MEAN implemented in Candle.
- Input: 10-dim edge features (length, oneway flag + 8 padding)
- Layer 1: `SAGEConv(10 → 64)` 
- Layer 2: `SAGEConv(64 → 64)`

**How GraphSAGE works here:**
1. **Line-graph construction:** Roads become nodes, junctions become edges
2. **Neighbor aggregation:** For each road segment, mean-pool its adjacent road segments' features
3. **SAGEConv forward:** `output = linear_l(self_features) + linear_r(aggregated_neighbors)`
4. Two layers with ReLU between them

**Output:** `Vec<RoadEmbedding>` — one 64-dim vector per road segment.

**Current state:** Falls back to empty embeddings if `models/graph_embed.safetensors` is missing.

---

### 6. NLP Query Parser (`core::nlp`)

**Purpose:** Convert natural language routing requests into structured VRP JSON.

**Two modes:**

**Rule-based** (`parse_query()`) — always available:
- Regex entity extraction: numbers ("50 packages"), coordinates ("45.5,-73.6"), times ("by 5pm"), capacity, speed
- Keyword intent classification: "sweep" → CPP, "time window" → CVRPTW, "package" → CVRP
- Template JSON generation with slot filling

**LLM-based** (`QwenNLParser`, gated behind `feature = "ml"`):
- Loads `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` from Hugging Face Hub via Candle
- System prompt: "Convert routing query to VRP JSON"
- Autoregressive generation with chat template (`<|im_start|>system...user...assistant`)
- 30s timeout, 256 max tokens

---

### 7. Legacy Rule-Based Scoring (`ml_legacy`)

**Purpose:** Deterministic fallback that works without any model files.

**Key functions:**
- `predict_solver()` — Scores 5 solvers with hand-tuned heuristics (density > 5 → default wins, tight capacity → Clarke-Wright, many vehicles → sweep, etc.)
- `score_route()` — Post-solve quality scoring on 4 dimensions:
  - **Distance efficiency** — star-tour lower bound vs actual
  - **Load balance** — max deviation from mean stop count per route
  - **Turn quality** — penalizes U-turns (×2), lefts (×0.3), rights (×0.1)
  - **Coverage** — fraction of stops assigned
  - **Overall** — weighted composite (35/25/20/20)

---

### Data Flow (how they connect)

```
User Input
    │
    ├── NLP Query ──→ nlp::parse_query() ──→ VRP JSON
    │
    └── JSON Task ──→ agent::run()
                        │
                        ▼
            ml::features::InstanceFeatures::from_input(input)
                        │
                        ├──→ ml::selector::predict_solver() ──→ best solver ID
                        │
                        ├──→ ml::quality_predictor::predict_quality() ──→ gap estimate
                        │
                        └──→ ml::automl::predict_hyperparams() ──→ solver params
                                        │
                                        ▼
                              Spawn solver with best config
                                        │
                                        ▼
                              ml_legacy::score_route() ──→ quality feedback
```

### Architecture Philosophy

| Principle | Implementation |
|-----------|----------------|
| **Graceful degradation** | Every learned module falls back to rule-based if model missing |
| **Pure Rust inference** | Candle runs on CPU/CUDA/Metal; no Python runtime needed |
| **Research-backed** | Features drawn from RouteFinder (2024), RRNCO (2025), Instance-Aware Parameter Configuration (2026), GAIN (2021) |
| **Offline training, online inference** | Models trained in Python (PyTorch) → exported to safetensors → loaded by Candle |
| **Deterministic** | No randomness in production inference; fixed seed where needed |

function.name: bash
function.description:
Run a shell command on the local machine and return stdout/stderr.

IMPORTANT: Do NOT use bash for file operations — use the dedicated tools instead:
- To read files: use read (not cat/head/tail)
- To edit files: use edit (not sed/awk)
- To write files: use write (not echo/cat <<EOF)

Commands run in a shell at the working directory. Each invocation is independent.
Chain dependent commands with &&. Independent commands should be separate bash calls (they can run in parallel).

For long-running commands (training, evaluation), run in the background and poll:
  nohup <command> > /tmp/output.log 2>&1 & echo $!
Then check status:
  kill -0 <PID> 2>/dev/null && echo 'running' || echo 'done'
  tail -n 50 /tmp/output.log

Timeout default 120s, max 36000s.

function.name: read
function.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. Returns contents with line numbers (cat -n format).

Usage:
- By default, reads up to 2000 lines from the beginning of the file.
- You can optionally specify offset and limit for large files, but prefer reading the whole file first.
- Lines longer than 4000 chars are truncated.
- Cannot read directories — use bash with 'ls' instead.
- You should read multiple potentially useful files in parallel when possible.
- IMPORTANT: Always read a file before editing or overwriting it. The edit and write tools will reject operations on files you haven't read.

path.description: Absolute path to the file to read.

offset.description: The line number to start reading from (1-based). Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

function.name: write
function.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem. Overwrites the existing file if one exists at the path.

- If this is an existing file, you MUST use the read tool first. This tool will fail if you did not read the file first.
- ALWAYS prefer editing existing files with the edit tool over overwriting with write.
- Creates parent directories as needed.

path.description: Absolute path to the file to write.

content.description: The complete file content to write.

function.name: edit
function.description:
Performs string replacements in files. Supports exact matching with fuzzy fallback.

Usage:
- You must read the file at least once before editing. This tool will error if you attempt an edit without reading the file.
- The edit will FAIL if old_str is not unique in the file. Either provide a larger string with more surrounding context to make it unique, or set replace_all to true.
- old_str and new_str must differ.
- Preserve indentation exactly as it appears in the file.
- Do NOT include line number prefixes from read output in old_str or new_str.
- To delete code, set new_str to empty string.
- Use replace_all for renaming variables or strings across the file.

Modes:
- replace (default): replace first occurrence of old_str with new_str.
- append_after: insert new_str immediately after old_str (old_str is kept).
- prepend_before: insert new_str immediately before old_str (old_str is kept).

path.description: Absolute path to the file to edit.

old_str.description: The text to find in the file. Must match exactly (fuzzy matching is used as fallback).

new_str.description: The replacement text. For append_after/prepend_before modes, the text to insert.

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_str (default: false).

- **list**: List files with sizes and structure
- **read**: Read file content (text files only)
- **upload**: Upload content to repo (can create PR)
- **delete**: Delete files/folders (supports wildcards like *.tmp)

## Use when
- Need to see what files exist in a repo
- Want to read config.json, README.md, or other text files
- Uploading training scripts, configs, or results to a repo
- Cleaning up temporary files from a repo

## Examples
{"operation": "list", "repo_id": "meta-llama/Llama-2-7b"}
{"operation": "read", "repo_id": "gpt2", "path": "config.json"}
{"operation": "upload", "repo_id": "my-model", "path": "README.md", "content": "# My Model"}
{"operation": "upload", "repo_id": "org/model", "path": "fix.py", "content": "...", "create_pr": true}
{"operation": "delete", "repo_id": "my-model", "patterns": ["*.tmp", "logs/"]}

## Notes
- For binary files (safetensors, bin), use list to see them but can't read content
- upload/delete require approval (can overwrite/destroy data)
- Use create_pr=true to propose changes instead of direct commit

function.name: hf_repo_git
function.description:
Git-like operations on HF repos: branches, tags, PRs, and repo management.

## Operations
**Branches:** create_branch, delete_branch, list_refs
**Tags:** create_tag, delete_tag
**PRs:** create_pr, list_prs, get_pr, merge_pr, close_pr, comment_pr, change_pr_status
**Repo:** create_repo, update_repo

## Use when
- Creating feature branches for experiments
- Tagging model versions (v1.0, v2.0)
- Opening PRs to contribute to repos you don't own
- Reviewing and merging PRs on your repos
- Creating new model/dataset/space repos
- Changing repo visibility (public/private) or gated access

## Examples
{"operation": "list_refs", "repo_id": "my-model"}
{"operation": "create_branch", "repo_id": "my-model", "branch": "experiment-v2"}
{"operation": "create_tag", "repo_id": "my-model", "tag": "v1.0", "revision": "main"}
{"operation": "create_pr", "repo_id": "org/model", "title": "Fix tokenizer config"}
{"operation": "change_pr_status", "repo_id": "my-model", "pr_num": 1, "new_status": "open"}
{"operation": "merge_pr", "repo_id": "my-model", "pr_num": 3}
{"operation": "create_repo", "repo_id": "my-new-model", "private": true}
{"operation": "update_repo", "repo_id": "my-model", "gated": "auto"}

## PR Workflow
1. create_pr → creates draft PR (empty by default)
2. Upload files with revision='refs/pr/N' to add commits
3. change_pr_status with new_status='open' to publish (convert draft to open)
4. merge_pr when ready

## Notes
- PR status: draft (default), open, merged, closed
- delete_branch, delete_tag, merge_pr, create_repo, update_repo require approval
- For spaces, create_repo needs space_sdk (gradio/streamlit/docker/static)
- gated options: 'auto' (instant), 'manual' (review), false (open)
